title: FixtureCase
description: One test scenario: the set of source documents fed to a single reconciliation run, plus the ground truth the test harness asserts against. This manifest is the answer key — it is never shown to the model.

schemaVersion.description: Version of this contract the case was written against. Bump on any breaking schema change.

id.description: Stable identifier for the case, unique across the fixture corpus (e.g. `set-b-contradiction`).

title.description: Human-readable name, shown in test output.

scenario.description: Which of the three canonical scenarios this case exercises. `agreement`: sources corroborate, nothing disputed. `contradiction`: sources give conflicting answers to the same question. `poisoned`: one source is about a different entity with a similar name.

entity.description: The entity the profile is about. In a `poisoned` case this is the real subject, not the impostor.

documents.description: Source document files making up this case, as POSIX paths relative to the case file. Order is the order they are supplied to the model.

expect.description: Ground truth the harness asserts against. Written by hand when the fixtures are authored.

notes.description: Optional author notes about why this case exists. Never shown to the model or the renderer.

id.description: Lowercase identifier, unique within its own collection.

entity.description: The single (fictional) entity a case is about.

aliases.description: Other names the sources use for the same entity.

expectation.description: What a correct reconciliation of this case looks like.

questions.description: Every underlying question the sources answer, one entry each. This is the grouping ground truth: a run that emits more groups than there are questions has under-merged, fewer has over-merged.

requiredSourceIds.description: Source ids that must each support at least one claim in the output. Catches a run that silently drops an input document.

excludedSourceIds.description: Source ids whose content must NOT appear in the profile — the impostor documents in a `poisoned` case. A claim citing one of these is a test failure.

expectedQuestion.description: One underlying question the sources answer, and whether they agree on the answer.

question.description: The underlying question, phrased as a question. Matched semantically by the harness, not by string equality.

status.description: `agreed` when the sources answering this question are mutually consistent; `disputed` when at least two of them conflict.

sourceIds.description: Sources that answer this question. A `disputed` question is answered by at least two.

plantedFact.description: Optional. The fact deliberately planted here, in the author's words (e.g. 'src-01 says 2011, src-02 says December 2010').

allOf.description: A disputed question must be answered by at least two sources — a single source cannot conflict with itself.
